candidates.evidence: Only the working-folder name mentions InOCl; the spectrum does not confirm it and I have no reliable reference Raman data for InOCl. Three modes (155.3, 299.0, 352.8 cm-1) cannot be matched to a known material with any confidence, so this is a low-confidence placeholder, not an identification.

hint_reasoning: No material_hint was given (task = identify). The folder name contains 'InOCl', but that is not spectral evidence and I could not check it against a reference spectrum. Peak positions, widths and polarization were measured from the 18-angle parallel/crossed series (0-170 deg, 10 deg steps, 60-722 cm-1, 1 cm-1 step). The 155.3 cm-1 mode is strong and narrow and is parallel-only; 352.8 cm-1 is strong in parallel with 180-degree modulation; 299.0 cm-1 is weak and does not match any template. No set of assignments fits a specific known layered material well enough to name it.

peaks.assignment: unassigned; polarization is the fully-symmetric-type pattern (parallel constant, crossed zero)
peaks.source: Lorentzian fit to angle-mean parallel spectrum (peak height ~7770 counts, FWHM fixed to this value per angle). Per-angle parallel amplitudes 7427-8240 counts with ~200 counts error; constant fit chi2/dof 1.6 vs twofold 1.2 (not significant). Crossed amplitude 10 +/- 47 counts (zero). Interpretation that this matches an A-type mode in backscattering from the layer normal is inferred from the standard Raman selection rule (Loudon 1964, Adv. Phys. 13, 423).

Lorentzian fit to angle-mean parallel spectrum (height ~900 counts). Parallel amplitude is a lobe peaking near 35-40 deg, near zero at 90-150 deg, with a twofold fit chi2/dof 6.8 (constant rejected at 34). Crossed is weak and nonzero (about 330-530 counts depending on estimator) and does not follow any template (constant chi2/dof 4.2, twofold 4.6, fourfold 1.9 with the wrong sign for crossed). A joint shared-angle E-type model gives chi2/dof 5.5. Parallel and crossed are not both constant, so isotropic_both does not apply.

Lorentzian fit to angle-mean parallel spectrum (height ~2600 counts). Parallel amplitude I = 2593 - 586 cos2t - 1990 sin2t (twofold, 180-degree period, chi2/dof 1.8; constant chi2/dof 80), maximum near 127 deg, minimum near 37 deg. Crossed is weak (about 100-200 counts, under ~8% of parallel mean) with no clear modulation, so the crossed partner is only marginally detected.

properties.name: phase
properties.source: No reference spectrum for any candidate was available to compare against; three modes alone do not fix the phase.

properties.name: layers
properties.source: Data start at 60 cm-1 and no low-frequency interlayer (shear or breathing) mode is visible, so layer number cannot be inferred.

artifacts.type: cosmic_ray (single-point spike, crossed, 70 deg; 9516.9 counts vs neighbours ~0 and ~306-1395; excluded from fits)
zero-clipped points (2988 of 23868 exact zeros, ~12.5%, mostly in background; probably noise clipped at zero, which biases the background slightly upward and weak-peak amplitudes slightly)

citations: Loudon, R. (1964). The Raman effect in crystals. Advances in Physics 13(52), 423-482. Standard backscattering selection rules used to interpret the 155.3 cm-1 parallel-only pattern as fully-symmetric-type.
limits: Identification is not established. Three peaks at 155.3, 299.0 and 352.8 cm-1 are not enough to name a material, and I have no reliable reference Raman data for InOCl or other layered candidates. The folder name is the only hint for InOCl and was not used as evidence.
No Si substrate line is present (sample is suspended). The region around 520.7 cm-1 is flat (parallel 401 vs 409 background, crossed 432 vs 411), so no Si peak is reported.

The 299 cm-1 mode is noisy. The data sit on a background of about 450 counts with noise of a few hundred counts per point, and 12.5% of points are clipped to zero. The crossed-configuration amplitudes for 299 and 352.8 cm-1 are weak and estimator-dependent; the polarization classes for them are the least certain.

Two weak features were tested and not reported. A parallel feature near 593 cm-1 has an amplitude of 88 +/- 41 counts (about 2 sigma). Candidate features at 137, 165 and 240 cm-1 are not significant. Many weak features at 2-3 sigma in the crossed residual are consistent with noise.

Peak widths are 3-5 cm-1 at a 1 cm-1 step, so they are sampling- and resolution-limited. The instrument resolution is not given in the metadata, so the widths cannot be separated from the instrumental broadening. Crossed-configuration positions are poorly constrained (the mean-spectrum fit gave 354.8 +/- 0.7 cm-1 for the 353 mode).

Polarization classes assume the stated angle convention (0-170 deg, 10 deg steps) and an ideal analyser. Analyser leakage or depolarization is not characterized, so the weak crossed signal of the 352.8 cm-1 mode may be partly leakage; this cannot be separated from a true crossed component with these data.

The data cannot say whether the material is a monolayer, few-layer or bulk: no interlayer mode below 155 cm-1 is visible and the spectrum starts at 60 cm-1. Phase, defects and strain are also not determined.
